rows.w: Columbus's last true public market (est. 1876) — 30-plus merchants including the original Jeni's, Momo Ghar and Hoyo's, just off the Short North and Arena District.

rows.n: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams — North Market
rows.w: Jeni Britton Bauer launched Jeni's at the North Market in 2002; the grassy-buttermilk base and inventive flavors (Brambleberry Crisp, Brown Butter Almond Brittle) that turned a Columbus stall into a national brand.
Phenomenal Himalayan dumplings that put Columbus's huge Nepali-Bhutanese community on the map; the jhol momo swim in a spiced sesame broth. Featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives.

The friendly gateway to Columbus's Somali food scene (one of the largest Somali communities in the US): tender suqaar, crisp sambusas and rice served the traditional way with a banana. 'Hoyo' means mother.
Chef Josh Dalton's glass-kitchen tasting menu, reinvented every few months — repeatedly ranked Columbus's #1 restaurant since 2012.
The rare brewery that's also one of the city's best restaurants — award-winning beers (the coffee-and-vanilla Daybreak cream ale) alongside a serious downtown dining room.

North Market's Northern Vietnamese stall from Khanh Le and his mother Lan Pham (a North Market staple since 2010; earlier known as Lac Viet) — a from-scratch pho broth simmered 24 hours and crisp, balanced banh mi.

rows.n: Grange Insurance Audubon Center and Scioto Audubon Metro Park
rows.w: A LEED-Platinum birding center on the restored Whittier Peninsula wetlands, plus a 35-ft outdoor climbing wall and downtown skyline views. Free.
A six-acre downtown green built on the footprint of the old City Center mall — a restored 1914 carousel, free summer concerts, a Thursday farmers market and 200+ free events a year. Free.

rows.n: Union Station Arch at McFerson Commons
rows.w: The last surviving arch of Columbus's demolished 1897 Union Station (a Daniel Burnham design), rescued during the 1976 wrecking and re-erected as the centerpiece of the 2.2-acre McFerson Commons in the Arena District. Free.

The flagship of a system twice named National Library of the Year — its $30M 2016 daylight-flooded renovation (GUND Partnership), opening onto Topiary Park, won the Columbus Landmarks James B. Recchie Design Award. Free to wander.
Columbus's oldest park (donated 1851) in Victorian Village — a pond, fountain and gazebo, and host of the summer ComFest gathering.

rows.w: The historic district just east of the Short North — brick worker cottages and the redeveloped Jeffrey Park, now home to Seventh Son and Fox in the Snow. Address is the landmark Jeffrey Manufacturing office building.

A 19th-century German immigrant neighborhood of brick-paved streets and Italianate cottages — the largest privately funded historic district on the National Register. Address is the German Village Society Meeting Haus.
ph: E Beck Street brick houses in German Village

rows.w: The only congressionally designated national museum for veterans of every branch and era, in a sculptural 2018 concrete-arch building (Allied Works) on the Scioto's west bank, ringed by a memorial grove and rooftop sanctuary.
The 1927 Art Deco skyscraper that has defined the skyline for a century — 555 feet, now a hotel, lit in changing colors nightly.

rows.w: The restored home of humorist and New Yorker cartoonist James Thurber, now a literary center, museum and bookstore on a Jefferson Avenue historic row.

The oldest surviving theatre in central Ohio — opened 1896 as the 'Great Southern Fireproof Hotel and Opera House' after a run of downtown theatre fires, it hosted Sarah Bernhardt, Anna Pavlova and John Philip Sousa. CAPA restored it in a 14-month, $10M rebuild reopening in 1998.

rows.w: The 11-acre historic green at the heart of OSU's campus, framed by University Hall and Thompson Library and landscaped with Olmsted-brothers input — the campus 'living room.'

A 13-plus-mile paved riverside greenway from downtown's North Bank Park up through OSU and Clintonville to Worthington — the city's spine for cycling and running. Address is the southern North Bank Park trailhead.
A 60-plus-acre living plant collection across OSU's campus — ornamental Learning Gardens, a conifer and hosta collection and a Chartres-style labyrinth. Open dawn to dusk, free.

rows.w: Family-owned since 1942 and home of the Thurmanator, a monster double burger loaded with ham, bacon and three cheeses. TEMPORARILY CLOSED after an April 2026 electrical fire; owners have vowed to rebuild — call ahead before visiting.

A Columbus original that launched at the North Market in 2014 and built a devoted following (and a social mission) around its Nashville hot chicken. All central-Ohio locations closed in September 2025 — kept here for the record.
